text: Gold rose about 1.7% overnight to around $4,128, a two-week high, as the dollar and Treasury yields slipped after the midterms.
Silver gained about 1.2% to near $52.85, lagging gold this morning, so the gold/silver ratio ticked up to about 78.
The 10-year Treasury yield eased about 3 basis points to roughly 4.87% while the 2-year held near 4.58%, ahead of Friday's jobs report.
Nasdaq futures fell about 0.9% after disappointing results from Arm and Qualcomm, while S&P 500 futures were flat and Dow futures rose.
Brent crude steadied near $94 after Wednesday's 8.7% drop on hopes of a US-Iran deal, though no deal has been signed.
The dollar index was roughly flat near 101.6 after bouncing from 101.20, and USD/JPY held around 158.4.
SLV closed Wednesday up 5.17% at $47.16, and SQQQ closed down 2.78% at $41.56.
